newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse to maintain firm clip.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse to maintain firm clip.

text.p: The Brussels bourse, whipped up by volatility due to options and futures expiries and a Dow looking set to extend Friday's 40-point gain, is expected to maintain its firm pace ahead in coming weeks, dealers said.
The Bel-20 share index closed up 0.89 percent, or 16.55 points, at 1,8895.13 in heavy trade.

"Where is the volume coming from? I don't know, I expected December to be quiet with investors on the sidelines," said one trader. "The words of Alan Greenspan have been completely forgotten, and that was only two weeks ago". Greenspan said then that assets were overvalued, sparking a sharp sell-off.

Dealers said that as this was the last trading day on Belfox futures market of the current series of Bel-20 index options and futures, volume had been expected to be as high as it had been in November, but they were bemused at its actual size.
Volume of Belgian shares traded was 6.9 billion francs, almost the double of yesterday's already chunky 3.5 billion.

Dealers said Wall Street's renewed energy, closing 127 points higher on Thursday and seeing further gains on Friday, had caused investors to shrug off speculation that the U.S. market was in imminent trouble.
"If Wall Street keeps up this tempo, we could break (the) 1,900 (resistance level)," said a trader.
Activity was raised as steel maker Cockerill Sambre saw its last day of trading in the Bel-20. It is due to be replaced in the index by electronics firm Barco on Monday.
Cockerill closed down 0.88 percent at 112 francs with heavy volume of 1.86 million shares traded, while Barco gained 2.2 percent at 5,500 francs with volume at 1.96 million.

"Currently we are changing our recommendation for (Cockerill) to 'buy' because now the selling pressure has disappeared, making it possible for the share to rise again," said analyst Isabelle Defranne at broker Mignon, Hanart, Declerck.
"It's never good leaving the Bel-20 as Belgian funds are more or less linked to the Bel-20...and many (investors) get out (of the share)," said analyst Olivier Heuschling at Banque Bruxelles Lambert.
Steel cord and wire maker Bekaert regained some lost ground after a 1996 profit warning by the company due to increased competition from eastern European steel companies.
Bekaert closed up 5.12 percent at 19,500 francs, with dealers saying it would be difficult to break the 20,000 franc resistance barrier in the short term.
Bekaert announced a 1.6 to 1.8 billion restructuring plan to deal with competition and to help the firm expand into fast growing markets, like Latin America and Asia.
Elsewhere insurance group Fortis AG closed up 2.37 percent to 4,965 francs, after finalising the acquisition of Bank MeesPierson from Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV.
